name: Landscape Values of Urban Places (Tokyo)
description:
Method replication: participants see 20 street-level images, 10 from Kunitachi City and 10 from elsewhere in the Tokyo area. For each image they give their overall impression of the place (1 = bad to 4 = good), rate the paper's 18 landscape values ("These places are valuable because …", from Completely worthless to Extremely valuable) and say whether they know the place. The images are not the paper's stimuli (37 Google Street View images with a 60° view as in the paper, 2019–2025: 19 from Kunitachi City and 18 from the wider Tokyo area; views facing only walls, garages or blurred areas were removed).
Original study: Inoue, Manabe, Murayama & Koizumi (2022), "Landscape value in urban neighborhoods: A pilot analysis using street-level images", Landscape and Urban Planning 221, 104357. 200 Google Street View images (100 from the Fujimidai neighbourhood of Kunitachi, chosen to include well-known facilities such as the city hall, library and schools, and 100 from the Tokyo metropolitan area) were rated online by 109 Kunitachi residents and 1,621 other Tokyo-area residents, each seeing 10 Fujimidai and 10 other images in random order. Values were compared with the overall impression and with familiarity and personal attributes.
Differences from the original study: (1) new images, with Kunitachi images taken from across the city rather than chosen around Fujimidai's facilities; (2) the 10 Kunitachi images come first and the 10 other images second, instead of being mixed; (3) only gender, age group and place of residence are asked about the participant.
author: Inoue, Manabe, Murayama & Koizumi
